items.title: MAV Grid
items.text:
An open, parametric dovetail-groove grid and face-plate standard.

Read the Specification View on GitHub

items.title: Overview
items.text:
MAV Grid is a grid standard for things that hold other things: walls, benches, cabinets, boxes and racks. Swappable face plates sit on a 32 mm pitch, and the 14 degree dovetail grooves between them hold keys, hooks and fixtures. The same geometry can be 3D printed, routed in sheet goods or machined, and it comes in two depths (Small and Large) that share one opening.

This project publishes three things together:

  • The specification: numbered rules, decided values and the tests that prove them.
  • The schema: a machine-readable description of every parameter, published as JSON Schema.
  • The toolkit: a Python package with parameterized generators, a face plate catalogue, adapters to other grid systems, and exporters for STEP, STL, 3MF and GLB.

[!WARNING] MAV Grid is pre-release. The specification is a 0.10 draft, nothing has been cut, printed or measured yet, and the schema and generators are still being built.

items.title: Core values (spec 0.10 draft)
items.text:
Quantity (mm) Small Large Pitch 32 32 Wall angle from the face normal 14° 14° Groove opening 8.0 8.0 Face plate top, one cell 24.0 24.0 Groove depth = plate thickness 6.0 9.5 Groove bottom width 11.0 12.7

See the Specification section for the full list and how the values are maintained.

items.title: Installation
items.text: This page covers all supported installation methods for mav-grid.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
Before installing, ensure your system meets the following prerequisites:

Requirement Minimum Version Notes Python 3.11+ Required for all installation methods Package Manager pip, uv, or Hatch Required for dependencies Git 2.x Required for source installs Docker 24.x Optional — for containerized installs

[!NOTE] MAV Grid has not been published to PyPI or GHCR yet. Until the first release, use Install from Source.

items.title: Standard Installation
items.text:
If you need to install the package directly into an environment (e.g., for local development or testing), use pip or uv:

pip (Standard) 
```bash
pip install mav-grid
```
uv (Alternative) 
```bash
uv pip install mav-grid
```

items.title: Verify the Installation
items.text:
After installation, you can confirm it is available in your Python environment by running:

python -c "import mav_grid; print(mav_grid.__version__)"

You should see output similar to:

0.1.0

items.title: Install from Source
items.text:
To install the latest unreleased code directly from the repository and set up a local development environment:

git clone https://github.com/markurtz/mav-grid.git
cd mav-grid

# Sync the development environment (installs all groups and extras)
uv sync --all-groups --all-extras

# Or, optionally install specific groups/extras:
uv sync --group dev

[!TIP] This is the recommended setup for contributors looking to make changes to the source code.

items.title: Docker Installation
items.text:
A pre-built Docker image is available for containerized environments:

# Pull the latest image
docker pull ghcr.io/markurtz/mav-grid:latest

# Run a one-off command
docker run --rm ghcr.io/markurtz/mav-grid:latest python -c "import mav_grid; print(mav_grid.__version__)"

For a persistent, volume-mounted setup using Docker Compose, see the docker-compose.yml in the root of the repository.

items.title: Platform-Specific Notes
items.text:
macOS 
Python, `pip`, and `uv` work seamlessly on macOS. We recommend using `brew install uv` to get started.
Linux 
Use your distribution's package manager to install Python 3.11+ (e.g., `sudo apt install python3`).
Windows 
Ensure Python is added to your PATH during the Windows installer setup.

items.title: Upgrading
items.text:
To upgrade an existing installation to the latest release:

pip 
```bash
pip install --upgrade mav-grid
```
uv 
```bash
uv pip install --upgrade mav-grid
```

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: This page takes you from a fresh install to your first command. The schema and generators are not released yet, so for now the toolkit reports its version, the spec it targets and the state of each component.

items.title: Step 1 — Check the install
items.text:
mav-grid --version

mav-grid v0.1.0

items.title: Step 2 — See what the toolkit targets
items.text:
mav-grid info

The output names the specification version (0.10.0, draft), the output directory for generated files, and each component with its status.

items.title: Step 3 — Use it from Python
items.text:
from mav_grid import SPEC_VERSION, Settings

settings = Settings(output_dir="build/parts")
print(SPEC_VERSION, settings.output_dir)

items.title: Configure defaults
items.text:
Settings are read from, in order: constructor arguments, MAV_GRID__* environment variables, a .env file, and the [tool.mav_grid] table of pyproject.toml:

[tool.mav_grid]
output_dir = "cad/out"

items.title: Using CI/CD and GitHub workflows
items.text: This guide explains the continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines used in mav-grid. It outlines the standard pathways, development cycles, and what standards must be met to contribute to the repository.

items.title: Understand the architecture
items.text:
The repository utilizes a modular, standardized GitHub Actions architecture. Workflows are categorized into core lifecycle events (prefixed with pipeline-) and utility triggers (prefixed with util-).

Our CI/CD pipelines ensure that all code merged into the main branch meets strict code quality, type-safety, testing, and security standards.

items.title: Navigate standard development pathways
items.text: When contributing to this repository, your code will travel through the following pipeline stages.

items.title: 1. The pull request cycle (pipeline-development.yml)
items.text:
When you open a Pull Request against main, the pipeline-development.yml workflow is triggered. This is the primary gateway for all code changes.

What it enables:

  • Quality Gates: Runs code quality and formatting checks (hatch run python:lint, hatch run project:lint, hatch run oci:lint) and static type verification (hatch run python:types) to enforce consistent standards.
  • Security Audits: Scans for vulnerabilities in dependencies and code patterns using detect-secrets, pip-audit (via Python security checks), and trivy/dockle (via OCI security checks).
  • Testing: Runs the Python unit, integration, and OCI structure tests. The PR will be blocked from merging if any tests fail.
  • Documentation Previews: Verifies that the Zensical documentation can be built cleanly.

Validation Standards: Your PR must pass all checks before it can be merged. We require strict adherence to PEP 8/Ruff, Python type annotations, and all tests must pass with adequate coverage.

items.title: 2. Main branch validation (pipeline-main.yml)
items.text:
Once your PR is reviewed and merged into main, the pipeline-main.yml workflow acts as a secondary validation layer.

What it enables:

  • Full Test Suite: Runs unit, integration, and full end-to-end (e2e) tests to ensure the merged changes didn't introduce regressions.
  • Documentation Deployment: Builds and deploys the latest version of the documentation site to the gh-pages branch.
  • Sanity Checks: Re-runs quality and security checks on the finalized codebase.

items.title: 3. Nightly and weekly pipelines
items.text:
To catch configuration drift and conduct deeper analysis, we run scheduled workflows:

  • Nightly (pipeline-nightly.yml): Runs daily at 00:00 UTC. It performs extended regression testing, builds alpha container images, and does deep security analysis.
  • Weekly (pipeline-weekly.yml): Runs every Sunday at 00:00 UTC. Focused on dependency hygiene, checking for outdated constraints and ensuring the test suite is robust against external changes.

items.title: Manage releases (pipeline-release.yml)
items.text:
Releasing a new version can be done in two ways:

  1. Manual UI Trigger (Recommended): A maintainer triggers the CI — Release workflow manually via the GitHub Actions UI.

  2. Inputs: Requires entering a version tag matching strict semver (e.g., v1.2.0).

  3. Branch Constraints: Can only be started on the main branch or a releases/* branch. If triggered on any other branch or tag ref via workflow_dispatch, the workflow fails the init-gate job and exits.
  4. Process: The workflow runs all quality, testing, and integrity checks. If they pass, it automatically tags the current commit with the entered version and pushes it to origin.

  5. Unified Release Publishing: Pushing the tag using the job's GITHUB_TOKEN successfully creates the remote tag without triggering recursive pipeline runs. The publishing jobs (publish-python and publish-oci) then execute immediately within the same manual run as soon as the tagging step succeeds. No Personal Access Tokens (PATs) or manual trigger restarts are required.

  6. Direct Tag Push: When a maintainer pushes a v*.*.* tag (e.g., v1.2.0) directly to origin, the workflow is triggered on the tag ref.

  7. It performs a final, full verification of the entire test suite on the tag.

  8. It builds immutable Python packages (sdist and wheel).
  9. It attests the build provenance using OIDC.
  10. It publishes the artifacts to PyPI and the container image to the GitHub Container Registry (GHCR).

items.title: Release Security & Environments
items.text:
To prevent unauthorized releases, we implement a Gate Job pattern using two-stage approvals bound to the release GitHub Environment:

  • Required Reviewers & Dual Approval: Repository Administrators should configure the release environment under Settings -> Environments -> release to require approvals from designated release managers. The workflow requires two approvals: one at init-gate (to authorize starting the verification checks) and a second at release-gate (to authorize tagging and publishing after all verification gates have succeeded).
  • Deployment Branches & Early Fail: Set the deployment branch policy to Selected branches allowing only main, releases/*, and tag patterns (such as v* or refs/tags/v*) to run jobs under this environment. Additionally, init-gate performs shell validation checking that the ref is a valid version tag (e.g. v1.2.3) or that branch execution (main or releases/*) was explicitly triggered by workflow_dispatch. If these conditions are not met, init-gate fails immediately.
  • Unified Publishing Gate & Gate Job Pattern: The release-gate job validates all previous gates (quality-gate, functional-gate, integrity-gate, and e2e-gate) and propagates the default_python configuration output down a linear dependency chain: release-gate -> tag-release -> publish-python -> docs / publish-oci. This prevents GHA from requesting unnecessary additional approvals and simplifies job conditionals.
  • Publish Input Overrides: Configured publish-python (GitHub Release tag name), publish-oci (OCI image tag name), and docs (docs version folder name) to use ${{ github.event.inputs.version_tag || github.ref_name }}. Decoupled docs entirely from init-gate so that docs and publish-oci only depend on publish-python.

items.title: Utilize custom actions
items.text:
To maintain consistency and reduce duplication, our lifecycle pipelines rely on composite actions located in the .github/actions/ directory:

  • Python Environment:
  • python/tests: Orchestrates Python test suite execution (unit, integration, e2e).
  • python/quality: Defines the exact linting (Ruff) and type-checking (Mypy/Ty) commands.
  • python/build and python/publish: Standardizes Python package generation and PyPI distribution.
  • OCI Containers:
  • oci/tests: Runs OCI Container Structure Tests (CST).
  • oci/quality: Lint Dockerfiles with Hadolint and Docker Compose configurations.
  • oci/build and oci/publish: Builds and registers production-ready container images.
  • Project-wide Utilities:
  • project/quality: Enforces repository-wide guidelines (mdformat, yamlfix, taplo).
  • project/docs: Handles building MkDocs/Zensical sites.

By relying on these shared actions, we ensure that the exact same linting and test rules are applied whether you are testing a PR, running a nightly build, or deploying a release.

Next Steps:

  • See the Contributing Guide for details on how to set up your local environment.

items.title: Repository Layout
items.text: MAV Grid keeps the specification, the schema, the toolkit and the samples in one repository so that a change to a rule, its value, its schema and its geometry can land in one reviewed pull request. This guide explains where each part lives and how they depend on each other.

items.title: Directory map
items.text:
Path What lives there Licence spec/ Normative specification text, decided values (mav-grid-params.json), changelog. SHL-2.0 spec/schema/ JSON Schema generated from mav_grid.schema. Never edited by hand. SHL-2.0 samples/ Sample parameter files, validated against the schema in CI. SHL-2.0 src/mav_grid/ The Python toolkit. Apache-2.0 tests/ Unit, integration and end-to-end tests. Apache-2.0 examples/ Runnable examples, each with its own test. Apache-2.0 docs/ This documentation site (Zensical). Apache-2.0 scripts/ Developer and CI helper scripts. Apache-2.0 .github/ CI/CD pipelines and reusable actions. Apache-2.0

Files under spec/ and samples/, and all generated geometry, are hardware design material under the Solderpad Hardware Licence 2.0. Everything else is software under Apache 2.0.

items.title: Toolkit packages
items.text: Package Responsibility Status mav_grid.spec The spec version the toolkit targets. Present mav_grid.settings Runtime settings from arguments, MAV_GRID__* environment variables and [tool.mav_grid] in pyproject. Present mav_grid.logging Loguru logging, silent unless enabled. Present mav_grid.schema Pydantic models for every spec object; source of the JSON Schema. Planned mav_grid.generators Geometry built only from schema objects: panels, swap bases, plates, folds, keys, gauges. Planned mav_grid.plates Catalogue of face plate kinds with their parameters and generators. Planned mav_grid.adapters Cross-compatibility with other systems, each modelled from scratch from published or measured dimensions. Planned mav_grid.export STEP, STL, 3MF and GLB writers, each with a JSON sidecar holding parameters, spec version and claim line. Planned

items.title: How the pieces depend on each other
items.text:
spec/ (rules, decided values)
   │  the schema encodes the rules
   ▼
mav_grid.schema ──► spec/schema/*.json ──► samples/*.json (validated in CI)
   │
   ▼
mav_grid.generators ◄── mav_grid.plates, mav_grid.adapters
   │
   ▼
mav_grid.export ──► STEP / STL / 3MF / GLB + JSON sidecar

The rules are the source of truth. The schema is the only place values enter the code, so generators never hard-code a dimension. A change to a decided value updates the rule text, the changelog, spec/mav-grid-params.json and, once the schema exists, the schema defaults, in the same pull request.

items.title: Open implementation choices
items.text:
These are left to the work that implements each package:

  • Geometry kernel: CadQuery or build123d (both OpenCascade based). It will be an optional cad extra so the schema installs without a CAD kernel.
  • Registries for plates and adapters: a registry with discriminated unions (for example with disdantic) would let new plate kinds and adapters register themselves and appear in the schema automatically.
  • Generated outputs: written to build/mav-grid/ locally and attached to releases, not committed.

items.title: mav_grid
items.text:
MAV Grid: an open, parametric dovetail-groove grid and face-plate standard.

This package is the reference toolkit for the MAV Grid specification. It is organised around the pieces the specification defines:

  • :mod:mav_grid.schema: Pydantic models and JSON Schema for every parameter.
  • :mod:mav_grid.generators: parameterized geometry built from schema objects.
  • :mod:mav_grid.plates: the catalogue of face plate kinds.
  • :mod:mav_grid.adapters: cross-compatibility with other grid systems.
  • :mod:mav_grid.export: STEP, STL, 3MF and GLB writers with JSON sidecars.

The subpackages are placeholders in this release; see the documentation for the roadmap.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Bases: BaseSettings

Central configuration store for the MAV Grid toolkit.

Generators, exporters and the CLI read their defaults from this model so a project can pin them once in pyproject.toml or the environment.

Source code in src/mav_grid/settings.py 
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """Central configuration store for the MAV Grid toolkit.

    Generators, exporters and the CLI read their defaults from this model so a
    project can pin them once in ``pyproject.toml`` or the environment.
    """

    model_config: ClassVar[SettingsConfigDict] = SettingsConfigDict(
        extra="ignore",
        populate_by_name=True,
        validate_assignment=True,
        env_prefix="MAV_GRID__",
        env_file=".env",
        pyproject_toml_table_header=("tool", "mav_grid"),
    )

    project_root: Path = Field(
        default_factory=Path.cwd,
        description="Root directory used to resolve relative paths.",
    )
    output_dir: Path = Field(
        default=Path("build/mav-grid"),
        description="Directory where generated geometry and sidecars are written.",
    )
    samples_dir: Path = Field(
        default=Path("samples"),
        description="Directory holding sample parameter files.",
    )

    @classmethod
    def settings_customise_sources(
        cls,
        settings_cls: type[BaseSettings],
        init_settings: PydanticBaseSettingsSource,
        env_settings: PydanticBaseSettingsSource,
        dotenv_settings: PydanticBaseSettingsSource,
        file_secret_settings: PydanticBaseSettingsSource,
    ) -> tuple[PydanticBaseSettingsSource, ...]:
        """Order the configuration sources by priority.

        :param settings_cls: The settings class being constructed.

def configure_logger(settings: LoggingSettings | None = None) -> None:
    """Apply logging settings to the ``mav_grid`` logger.

    :param settings: Options to apply; read from the environment when omitted.
    :returns: None
    """
    settings = settings or LoggingSettings()
    logger.remove()
    if not settings.enabled:
        logger.disable("mav_grid")
        return
    logger.enable("mav_grid")
    logger.add(sys.stderr, level=settings.level, format=settings.format)

Logging setup for the MAV Grid toolkit, built on Loguru.

The library stays silent by default. Applications and the CLI call :func:configure_logger to turn output on.

Example

.. code-block:: python

from mav_grid.logging import LoggingSettings, configure_logger, logger

configure_logger(LoggingSettings(enabled=True, level="DEBUG"))
logger.debug("generator started")

items.title: mav_grid.settings
items.text:
Runtime settings for the MAV Grid toolkit.

Settings are resolved, in priority order, from constructor arguments, environment variables prefixed with MAV_GRID__, a .env file, and the [tool.mav_grid] table of the pyproject.toml in the project root.

Example

.. code-block:: python

from mav_grid.settings import Settings, get_settings

settings = Settings(output_dir="build/parts")
assert settings.output_dir.name == "parts"

global_settings = get_settings()
print(global_settings.project_root)

class Settings(BaseSettings):

        pyproject_toml_table_header=("tool", "mav_grid"),

        default_factory=Path.cwd,
        description="Root directory used to resolve relative paths.",
    )
    output_dir: Path = Field(

    )

    )

items.title: mav_grid.adapters
items.text:
Cross-compatibility adapters for MAV Grid (placeholder).

Adapters map other systems onto the MAV Grid lattice, for example Gridfinity, openGrid, MFT/3 style benches, System 32, French cleats, T-slot extrusion, pegboard, DIN rail and rack units. Each adapter will declare the target system, its pitch, its licence terms and the support level it reaches.

Every adapter is modelled from scratch from published or measured dimensions. No geometry is copied from another system's files.

items.title: mav_grid.export
items.text:
File exporters for MAV Grid geometry (placeholder).

This subpackage will write generated geometry to STEP, STL, 3MF and glTF (GLB) files, together with a JSON sidecar that records the parameters, the spec version and the claim line for each part.

items.title: mav_grid.generators
items.text:
Parameterized geometry generators for MAV Grid (placeholder).

This subpackage will turn validated schema objects from :mod:mav_grid.schema into solid geometry: grooved panels and swap bases, face plates of any span, folds, columns, boxes, keys and test gauges. Each generator takes only schema models as input so that every output is reproducible from a parameter file.

The geometry kernel is not chosen yet (CadQuery and build123d are the candidates); it will be added as an optional cad extra so the schema stays installable without a CAD kernel.

items.title: mav_grid.plates
items.text:
Face plate catalogue for MAV Grid (placeholder).

Face plates are the core object of MAV Grid spec 0.10: they sit between the grooves and carry the features (plain panels, lids, hooks, bins and cross-compatibility patterns). This subpackage will register each plate kind with its parameters, its validation rules and the generator that draws it.

items.title: mav_grid.schema
items.text:
Parameter schema for MAV Grid (placeholder).

This subpackage will hold the Pydantic models that describe every MAV Grid object in machine-readable form: the core grid (pitch, lattice, groove profiles for the Small and Large sizes), face plates and their spans, edges and margins, corners and folds, holes and fixings, fits, and claim lines. The models are the single source of truth for the JSON Schema published under spec/schema/ and for validating sample files under samples/.

Planned layout:

  • core.py: grid pitch, lattice, groove profile, size variants.
  • plates.py: face plate geometry, spans, fixings, clearances.
  • structures.py: edges, margins, folds and corners.
  • claims.py: conformance claim lines and support levels.
  • export.py: JSON Schema generation for spec/schema/.

Nothing is implemented yet; the spec 0.10 draft is the reference until the schema lands.

items.title: Specification
items.text: The MAV Grid specification defines the grid, the grooves, the face plates and everything that attaches to them, as numbered rules that a part either meets or does not. The normative files live in the spec/ directory of the repository.

items.title: Status
items.text: The current version is 0.10.0 (draft). It adopts the B2 dimensions decided on 2026-11-19 and makes the face plate the core object. Nothing has been cut, printed or measured yet, so every fit is a calculation and is tagged Unproven until its test passes.

items.title: Decided values
items.text:
Quantity Value Pitch 32 mm Lattice 8 mm Wall angle 14° from the face normal Groove opening 8.0 mm Face plate top 24.0 mm for one cell; 32c − 8 by 32r − 8 for c × r cells Small groove 6.0 mm deep, 11.0 mm bottom Large groove 9.5 mm deep, 12.7 mm bottom Cell hole 5.0 mm; M6 house thread, M5 and ¼-20 as named variants Height step 8 mm Plate clearance judged by gauge, starting at 0.15 mm per side Preferred spans 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 3, 6, 12 cells

Edges sit on a grid line with a 4.0 mm half groove or carry a declared plain margin of any width. Corners are solid: nothing targets a corner, and parts that cross a fold hold in the grooves on each side. There are no locating pins; loose plates fix with one screw through the cell hole.

The machine-readable copy of these values is spec/mav-grid-params.json. A test in the suite checks that the values stay consistent with each other (for example, that the plate top plus the opening equals the pitch, and that each groove bottom follows from its depth and the wall angle).

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Rule IDs carry a section prefix: C- core, P- plates, S- corners and structures, H- keys and hardware, F- fits, A- compatibility, K- claims, L- loads, V- versions.
  • Tags: every rule is Decided (with a date) or Unproven.
  • Keywords: MUST, SHOULD and MAY follow RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.
  • Versioning: the specification follows Semantic Versioning, separately from the Python package.

items.title: Schema
items.text: The JSON Schema for parameter files will be generated from the mav_grid.schema models and published under spec/schema/. See Repository Layout for how the pieces fit together.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: See the specification changelog.

items.title: 0.10.0 (draft, 2026-11-20)
items.text:
• Face plates become the core object. Grooves exist only where two plates meet, so 32 mm is the minimum groove spacing.
  • B2 dimensions: 8.0 mm opening, 24.0 mm single-cell plate top, 14 degree walls. Small is 6.0 mm deep with an 11.0 mm bottom; Large is 9.5 mm deep with a 12.7 mm bottom.
  • Corners are solid. Nothing targets a corner; parts that cross a fold hold in the grooves on each side.
  • Any edge may carry a declared plain margin of any width.
  • No locating pins. Loose plates fix with one screw through the 5.0 mm cell hole; M6 house thread with M5 and ¼-20 variants.
  • Plate clearance is judged by gauge, starting at 0.15 mm per side.

items.title: 0.9 (superseded, 2026-11-15)
items.text: • Channel-first design with gated decision levels. Superseded by 0.10.
